empfangen.status.bereit: Ready. Start the microphone or load a WAV file.
empfangen.status.dateiende: End of file, no header found.
empfangen.status.verworfen: Header for {modus} found, but no usable signal. Discarded.

senden.editor: Image to send inside the mode frame. Dragging moves the image or a text field, pinch and mouse wheel zoom.
senden.hinweis: Choose an image or take a photo. Move the section with one finger, pinch to zoom. Text fields can be dragged as well.
senden.pegel.hinweis: The signal always has headroom (at most 80 % of full scale). Set the device volume so the transmitter does not overdrive.
senden.fehler.audio: The signal cannot be created or played: {grund}
senden.fsk: Send callsign as FSK ID after the image
senden.fsk.leer: Enter your callsign under “Details for placeholders” to send the ID.
senden.cal: Send calibration header before the leader tone
senden.cal.info: Adds {dauer} s of fixed tones before the leader tone, the way QSSTV sends them. Not needed for reception, but gives the transmitter (for example VOX) a moment of lead-in.
senden.vorlage.hinweis: A template remembers position, size, colour and font of all texts, placeholders included. An existing name is overwritten.
senden.vorlage.name: Template name
senden.vorlage.fehler.name: Give the template a name.
senden.vorlage.fehler.leer: There is no text on the picture yet, nothing to save.
senden.vorlage.fehler.voll: At most {n} templates are possible. Delete one or use the name of an existing one to overwrite it.
senden.rapport.s: The ? in the report stands for S. Replace it with the signal strength from the S-meter (1 to 9), otherwise the question mark ends up in the picture.
senden.takt.info: Clock correction of this device: {ppm} ppm (Settings). Applies to playback, not to WAV files.
galerie.leer: No images yet. Received images are saved here automatically, including partial ones.
galerie.zip.fertig.log: Backup with {n} image(s) and {q} QSO(s) saved ({groesse}).
galerie.eingelesen.log: {neu} image(s) and {q} QSO(s) restored, {uebersprungen} image(s) and {qUebersprungen} QSO(s) already present.
log.hinweis: Your QSOs with time in UTC, report and band. Export as ADIF for your station log or as CSV. Entries live in this browser. The full ZIP backup of the gallery includes the log.
log.leer: No QSO logged yet. In the image viewer, “Add to log” takes callsign, mode, time and report from the picture.
log.f.name: Name
log.fehler.call: Please enter a valid callsign (letters, digits, slash).
log.fehler.locator: The locator is invalid (for example JO50 or JO50ab).
galerie.versch.hinweis: Without a VIS header the start of the picture is only estimated: the first line heard counts as the top. If the true start lies higher up, shift the picture down (positive values, the top stays empty). If the top lines already belong to something else, shift up (negative values). The original is kept, you can always go back.
galerie.speicher.info: {n} image(s), {bilder} in the gallery. The browser uses {nutzung} of {kontingent} in total.
galerie.dauerhaft.ja: Storage is persistent: the browser will not clear it on its own.
galerie.dauerhaft.nein: Storage is not persistent. The browser may clear it when space runs low. Request persistent storage or make backups.
galerie.dauerhaft.unbekannt: The browser does not say whether storage is persistent. Make a backup now and then.
galerie.dauerhaft.abgelehnt: The browser did not grant persistent storage. In Chrome, installing the app often helps.
empfangen.status.blind: Detected from the line timing without a VIS header, the top of the picture may be shifted.
empfangen.rapport.hinweis: As a three-digit report (RSV): {rsv}. The app suggests R and V from the picture, S is preset to 9. Enter the signal strength from the S-meter there, the app cannot measure it.
empfangen.rapport.s: Signal strength S from the S-meter
rapport.info.intro: In SSTV the report has three digits: R for the readability of the text, S for the signal strength and V for the picture quality. 595 is the dream report: text perfectly readable, signal S9, picture excellent.
rapport.info.r.3: 3: readable only with considerable effort and some guessing
rapport.info.r.2: 2: hardly readable, only fragments of letters
rapport.info.r.1: 1: completely unreadable, the writing cannot be made out in the noise
rapport.info.s.text: You read the signal strength on your receiver’s S-meter, from S1 (signal barely above the noise) to S9. The app cannot measure it: it only hears the audio behind the receiver, not the field strength at the antenna.
rapport.info.v.5: 5: excellent, noise-free as if straight from the graphics program
rapport.info.v.4: 4: good, clear picture with few disturbances
rapport.info.v.3: 3: fair, the content is easy to make out, but the noise is obvious
rapport.info.v.2: 2: poor, only rough outlines and heavy interference stripes
rapport.info.v.1: 1: barely perceptible, the picture almost drowns in the noise
rapport.info.beispiele: Examples: 595 is a crystal-clear picture at S9. A weak signal fighting its way through a thunderstorm is more like 453 or 333. You write the report as a three-digit number in your reply, for example “UR RSV 584”. Note picture disturbances such as QRM, QRN or SLANT (slanted picture caused by the other station’s sound card) as well.
rapport.info.vorschlag.titel: How the app works out the suggestion
rapport.info.vorschlag.text: After the picture, the app measures how noisy it is (in the pixels themselves, not in the audio) and derives R and V from that. If many lines are missing, both values drop. The app does not know S: it is preset to 9, replace it with the value from the S-meter.
rapport.info.grenzen: This is an approximation. A photo with fine texture quickly counts as noisy, and the measurement cannot see slant or colour errors. The suggestion is an aid, the decision is yours.
empfangen.fehler.galerie: The image could not be saved to the gallery: {grund}
codierung.einleitung: Here you can see how an image becomes a sound. The app calculates all numbers and graphics from the mode table and the encoder, so they match what is really generated when you transmit. The listening samples let you hear the tones.
codierung.modus.hinweis: The mode applies to all three cards.
codierung.zeile.text: An SSTV image is sent line by line. Every line starts with a short sync pulse at 1200 Hz, followed by the picture points as tones. How the colours are packed depends on the mode.
codierung.zeile.martin: Martin sends the three colour channels one after another: green first, then blue, then red. The sync is at the start of the line and every channel has the full resolution. A short separator at 1500 Hz sits between the channels.
codierung.zeile.scottie: Scottie also sends green, blue and red one after another, but the sync is in the middle of the line, between blue and red. That is why the line starts before the sync here, and the time before it is negative.
codierung.zeile.robot36: Robot 36 saves time with YCrCb: every line carries the brightness (Y) at full resolution and one colour difference in half the time. The separator says which: 1500 Hz in even lines (R−Y), 2300 Hz in odd lines (B−Y). The receiver uses each colour difference for two lines.
codierung.zeile.robot72: Robot 72 works like Robot 36 with YCrCb, but every line carries both colour differences: first the brightness (Y), then R−Y and finally B−Y, each in half the time of the brightness. A separator at 1500 Hz sits before R−Y and one at 2300 Hz before B−Y. In exchange the line takes twice as long as Robot 36, and every line has its own colour.
codierung.zeile.pd: PD sends two image lines in one transmitted line: first the brightness of the first line (Y0), then the colour differences R−Y and B−Y, which apply to both lines, and finally the brightness of the second line (Y1).
codierung.zeile.wraase: After the sync and a very short porch, Wraase SC2-180 sends red, green and blue back to back with no separator between them. Every colour channel has the full resolution and takes 235 ms.
codierung.zeile.regler: Point in time within the line
codierung.zeile.balken: Structure of one line of {modus}, {ms} long, to scale
codierung.cursor.sync: {ms} after the start of the sync: sync pulse, {hz} Hz. This is how the receiver finds the start of the line.
codierung.cursor.porch: {ms} after the start of the sync: short pause (porch) at {hz} Hz.
codierung.cursor.sep: {ms} after the start of the sync: separator at {hz} Hz.
codierung.cursor.scan: {ms} after the start of the sync: {kanal}, picture point {pixel} of {n}. It lasts {us} µs, and its tone lies between 1500 and 2300 Hz depending on the brightness.
codierung.zeile.fakten: One line takes {zeile}. The image has {pakete} transmitted lines for {zeilen} image lines of {breite} points each and takes {bild} s, {gesamt} s with the preamble.
codierung.zeile.rueck: The decoder first looks for the sync pulses and derives the start and rhythm of the lines from them. Then it measures, for every picture point, the mean frequency over its duration ({pixel} µs at {breite} points). A small clock error of the sound card skews the lines, and the app corrects it using all sync pulses.
codierung.freq.text: Every brightness has its tone, like the keys of a piano. Black sends 1500 Hz, white 2300 Hz, and the frequency rises evenly in between. The 800 Hz span is divided into 256 steps, about 3.1 Hz each. The sync at 1200 Hz is lower than any black, so the receiver cannot confuse it with a picture point.
codierung.freq.rgb: {modus} sends RGB: black (0) is {schwarz} Hz, white (255) is {weiss} Hz.
codierung.freq.ycc: {modus} sends YCrCb in studio range: black is Y = {y1} at {hz1} Hz, white is Y = {y2} at {hz2} Hz. Pure black therefore does not appear at 1500 Hz.
codierung.freq.rueck: The decoder converts the measured frequency back into a value: (frequency − 1500) times 255 divided by 800. If the receiver is tuned wrongly, all tones shift by the same amount. In RGB modes the picture gets brighter or darker; in YCrCb modes the colours tip over, towards pink when too high and towards green when too low. The app measures the offset on the leader tones and the sync and removes it.
codierung.vis.text: Before the picture, the signal tells which mode follows: this is the VIS code (Vertical Interval Signaling). It consists of a leader tone at 1900 Hz, a short break at 1200 Hz, another leader tone and ten bits of 30 ms each. A 1 sounds at 1100 Hz, a 0 at 1300 Hz, and start and stop bit are at 1200 Hz.
codierung.vis.zahl: {modus} has the VIS number {vis}. Written in binary with the most significant bit first, that is {binaer}.
codierung.vis.gesendet: The least significant bit is sent first: {bits}. Then comes the parity bit {par}. It makes the number of ones even (here {einsen}). If interference flips a bit, the parity no longer matches and the receiver discards the code.
codierung.vis.rueck: The decoder looks for the leader tone and compares the VIS block with a template, which is reliable even with noise. It reads the frequency offset from the two leader tones. If the code is missing, for example because the recording starts too late, it recognises the mode from the rhythm of the sync pulses.
labor.einleitung: The lab helps with troubleshooting. Start the microphone first, then the level test, tuning aid and clock measurement show their values live. The noise simulator needs no microphone, it calculates everything inside the app.
labor.audio.text: The microphone runs without echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain so that the measurements are right. The test tone is a sine of exactly 1900 Hz.
labor.ton.hinweis: You need the test tone for the clock measurement (on device A) and for the distance to the noise floor. Keep the volume moderate, 20 to 40 % is usually enough.
labor.pegel.text: Shows how hard the microphone signal is driven. For SSTV a peak between about −20 and −6 dBFS is good. At 0 dBFS the signal is clipped, below −30 dBFS it is too quiet and noise dominates.
labor.pegel.aus: Start the microphone to measure the level.
labor.pegel.grund: Noise floor (quietest moment of the last 10 s)
labor.pegel.hinweis.zuleise: Too low: raise the gain or turn the source up.
labor.pegel.hinweis.zulaut: Clipping: lower the gain. If the peak still sits at 0 dBFS, lower the microphone level in the system or the volume of the source.
labor.pegel.hinweis.hoch: High: not clipping yet, but little headroom. Turn it down a step if peaks get closer to 0 dBFS.
labor.abst.text: Measures the frequency of the strongest tone and shows by how many Hz it differs from the chosen target tone. On air, tune the receiver so that the leader tone sits at 1900 Hz. That also removes the colour cast in Robot and PD. In USB the tone drops when you raise the receive frequency.
labor.abst.keinton: No clear tone near the target tone.
labor.abst.gut: Right on: the deviation is 5 Hz at most.
labor.abst.zuhoch: The tone is {hz} Hz too high.
labor.abst.zutief: The tone is {hz} Hz too low.
labor.takt.text: Measures how far the clocks (sample rates) of two devices drift apart. This causes the skew of the lines, which the decoder compensates.
labor.takt.ablauf: How it works: device A plays the test tone (card above, “Start test tone”). Device B listens with its microphone and starts the measurement here. After about 10 seconds a value appears, after a minute it is accurate.
labor.takt.bereit: Ready. Start the measurement as soon as the test tone is playing.
labor.takt.keinton: No stable test tone at 1900 Hz. Play it on device A, not too quietly.
labor.takt.misst: Measuring … about {s} s until the first value.
labor.takt.ergebnis: Measuring time {s} s, mean frequency {hz} Hz, uncertainty about ±{plusminus} ppm, spread {streu} Hz. {deutung}
labor.takt.deutung.klein: The clocks run almost the same.
labor.takt.deutung.normal: This is a usual value for sound cards.
labor.takt.deutung.gross: That is unusually large. The decoder compensates for it, but without compensation the picture would be skewed.
labor.takt.ton.weg: (The test tone can no longer be heard stably.)
labor.takt.grenzen: Positive means: the clock of device A runs faster than that of device B. If the test tone plays on the same device that records with its microphone, both share the same clock and you see almost 0 (a self test). On air the tuning error of the receivers comes on top; this card does not measure that, use the tuning aid for it.
labor.takt.uebernehmen: Use as correction for this device
labor.takt.uebernommen: Saved: {ppm} ppm. The app compensates this when sending (Settings, Send section).
labor.takt.uebernehmen.hinweis: This is only right if device A is accurate (for example a PC with a good clock). If A is off itself, its error ends up in your correction. Applies to playback from the app only, not to WAV files. Receiving needs nothing: the decoder compensates the clock rate itself.
labor.sim.text: Encodes a test image, adds noise, tuning error and clock error, and decodes it with the decoder of the app. This shows how much interference a mode can take. Everything runs on your device.
labor.sim.snr: Signal-to-noise ratio in the SSTV band
labor.sim.falsch: A different mode was recognised, the image counts as lost.
labor.sim.verloren: Nothing recognised: the signal is too disturbed.
labor.sim.vergleich.fertig: Comparison done at {snr}, tuning error {versatz} Hz, clock error {takt} ppm.
labor.sim.rueck: The signal-to-noise ratio refers to a band of 2400 Hz, about the width of an SSTV channel. On real radio paths interference is distributed differently (fading, impulse noise). The simulator is a comparison tool, not a copy of reality.
settings.call.hinweis: Used when sending as the placeholder {call} in text fields and as the FSK ID after the image.
settings.call.warn: This does not look like a callsign. Letters, digits and the slash are allowed, 3 to 12 characters.
settings.locator.hinweis: Maidenhead locator with 4, 6 or 8 characters, for example JO50 or JO50ab. Placeholder {loc}.
settings.locator.warn: Invalid locator. Expected for example JO50 or JO50ab (first two letters A to R, then digits, then letters A to X).
settings.autospeichern.hinweis: Finished and aborted images go to the gallery, partial images are marked.
settings.roh: Keep the raw recording of received pictures
settings.roh.hinweis: Attaches the recording (12 kHz, 16 bit, with a little lead-in) to every picture received through the microphone. In the gallery you save it as a WAV and can decode the picture again later in “Receive” (load WAV file) or with another program, for example with different brightness. Robot 36 needs about 1 MB, Scottie DX about 6.5 MB.
settings.ohnevis: Detect pictures without a VIS header
settings.ohnevis.hinweis: If the app finds no VIS header, it looks for a running picture in the line timing of the sync pulses. Fast modes are found after a few seconds, Scottie DX and PD180 need 20 to 25 seconds. The first lines are kept, but the top of the picture is only estimated. Costs some processing time and memory (about 6 MB).
settings.taktppm.hinweis: If the sound card runs too slow or too fast, everything sounds slightly too low or too high, and pictures come out slanted at the other end when their decoder does not compensate. The lab measures the value (clock deviation card). 0 means no correction.
settings.taktppm.warnung: Please enter a whole number between −2000 and 2000.
settings.helligkeit.hinweis: Robot 36 and PD send brightness and colour in studio range (black at Y = 16). Other decoders such as slowrx take Y directly as brightness, so their pictures look flatter and black shows as grey. This switch makes SSTV-Horch do the same, for comparing with other decoders. Applies from the next reception and only to Robot 36 and PD; saved pictures stay unchanged.
senden.station.leer: Enter your callsign and locator in the settings, then {call} and {loc} fill in by themselves.
galerie.auto.hinweis: You decide in the settings whether received images are saved automatically.
settings.locator.fertig: Calculated from your position: {loc} (accuracy about {genau} m). The position itself is not stored.
settings.locator.fehler.0: This device or browser does not provide a position. Enter the locator by hand.
settings.locator.fehler.1: Access to the location was denied. Allow it in the browser settings for this site or enter the locator by hand.
settings.locator.fehler.2: The position is not available right now. Try again outdoors or with location switched on.
settings.locator.fehler.3: Getting the position took too long. Try again.
senden.schrift.hinweis: Roboto, Roboto Mono and Montserrat are part of the app, system fonts look different on each device.
settings.locator.standort.lang: Calculate the locator from this device’s location
settings.zeit.hinweis: Applies to the gallery, file names and the placeholders {datum} and {zeit}. With UTC the text says “UTC”.
settings.audio.hinweis: The choice applies to Receive, Send, Lab and the listening samples. A virtual audio cable or a USB sound card shows up here as a device. If the chosen device is missing, the app uses the default device.
settings.audio.entsperren.hinweis: The browser shows device names only after you have allowed microphone access once. The microphone is released again right away.
settings.audio.ausgang.nein: Your browser cannot switch the audio output (Firefox cannot yet). Set it in the system.
empfangen.hinweis.geraet: The chosen microphone was not found, the default device is running.
senden.hinweis.bild: Drag the image to move the section. Two fingers or the mouse wheel zoom.
senden.texte.hilfe: Tap a text in the list to edit it. Move it in the image with your finger. Placeholders such as {call} are filled in when you transmit.
senden.texte.leer: No texts yet. Add one below.
about.purpose: Encode and decode SSTV pictures: send and receive over loudspeaker and microphone, plus a gallery and a lab to experiment in.
about.componentsNote: SSTV-Horch itself is licensed under the GPL-3.0 or later. It uses no libraries and no framework, only these third-party parts (the license texts are in the source code, folder fonts and LICENSE):
about.comp.montserrat: Typeface of the name in the drawer.
about.thanks1: Many thanks to the developers of QSSTV and slowrx, whose open sources served as a reference for modes, timings and cross-checks, and to the authors of the MMSSTV documentation.
about.thanks2: Thanks also to everyone who makes typefaces, icons and tools freely available. The technology behind SSTV is explained in the blog article “SSTV – Fernsehen im Schneckentempo” on ohrenbeisser.de (in German).
about.privacyText: All data stays on this device. There are no accounts and no analytics. Pictures and recordings are stored locally in the browser only. The links on the “WebSDR” page lead to third-party servers, whose operators are responsible for their privacy. The audio you take over from there stays on your device.
about.liability1: The app is provided without any warranty, as is (see GPL-3.0, sections 15 and 16). The author is not liable for damages arising from its use.
about.liability2: You are responsible for your own radio operation: callsign, frequency, transmit power, band plan and the terms of your amateur radio license. The app only plays sound through the speaker, it does not key a radio.
empfangen.status.hoertTab: Listening to the browser tab's audio and waiting for an SSTV code (VIS).
empfangen.fehler.tab.keinton: The chosen window delivered no audio. Pick a browser tab and tick “Share tab audio”.
websdr.intro: Here you listen to SSTV through someone else's receiver on the net (WebSDR, KiwiSDR, OpenWebRX) and let SSTV-Horch decode the picture. The picture appears in “Receive”. This page is still in testing (beta).
websdr.schritt1: Open one of the servers below. It opens in a new tab.
websdr.schritt2: Set the frequency and sideband there (for example 14.230 MHz, USB) and start the audio.
websdr.schritt3: Come back here and press “Use audio from a browser tab”. In the dialog choose the server's tab and keep “Share tab audio” ticked.
websdr.schritt4: SSTV-Horch switches to “Receive” and decodes. The tab has to stay open and must not be muted.
websdr.tab.knopf: Use audio from a browser tab
websdr.tab.laeuft: Audio from a tab is being received.
websdr.tab.nicht: This function is not available in this browser or on this device. It only works in Chrome or Edge on a computer.
websdr.server.hinweis: The servers belong to other people. Be considerate to the operators and do not leave the connection running for hours. Some servers allow only a limited number of listeners. Whether a server is reachable right now and what it covers, you only see when you open it.
websdr.s.twente.band: wide-band short wave, 20 m with 14.230 MHz USB
websdr.s.graz.band: separate receivers for 30 m, 20 m and 17 m, 20 m with 14.230 MHz USB
websdr.s.utah.band: 20 m with 14.230 MHz USB, omnidirectional antenna and a beam pointing east
websdr.s.goonhilly.band: VHF and UHF, FM. The ISS sends SSTV on 437.550 MHz FM, only during ARISS events
websdr.stand: The list is a suggestion as of {datum}. Servers come and go.
